description: Page headers, section heads, and table heads. A header is the thing a reader checks to know where they are, so its job is orientation before decoration - and its rhythm has to be the same on every surface, or the product reads as assembled from parts.

gates.title: Every Surface Uses The Same Header Rhythm
gates.rule: Title, then supporting chips or counts, then a spacer, then actions - in that order, at the same height and padding, on every page of the product. A header that reorders itself per section makes each section feel like a different application.
gates.fix: Extract one header component and compose the per-page differences as props.

gates.title: A Sticky Header Is Opaque And Layered
gates.rule: A header that sticks carries an opaque background, a bottom rule or shadow to separate it from what scrolls beneath, and a z-index from the named scale above in-page sticky elements.
gates.fix: Give the sticky header an opaque surface token, a bottom border, and the nav layer from the z-index scale.

gates.title: One Sticky Thing At The Top
gates.rule: A page header and a section header both sticking at top: 0 overlap, and the one deeper in the DOM paints over the other. Secondary sticky elements offset by the header's height.
gates.fix: Define a header height token and offset every secondary sticky element to it.

gates.title: The Header Does Not Shrink The Content Behind It
gates.rule: A fixed or sticky header reserves its height on the scrolling content, so the first row is not hidden underneath it on load or after an anchor jump.
gates.fix: Add scroll-margin-top on anchor targets and padding matching the header height on the scroll container.

gates.title: The Title Is The Loudest Thing In It
gates.rule: One h1 per page, at the top of the header, heavier and larger than everything beside it. A header where the action button outweighs the title tells the reader the button is where they are.
gates.fix: Set the title's weight and size above the chips and controls beside it.

gates.title: Header Counts Are Tabular
gates.rule: Counts and figures in a header use tabular figures, so the header does not reflow every time a number ticks.
gates.fix: Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to the count element.

gates.title: Header Actions Are Right, Title Is Left
gates.rule: Title and context on the leading edge, actions on the trailing edge, separated by a flexible spacer rather than a fixed margin. Actions that drift with the title's length are actions the reader has to hunt for.
gates.fix: Put a flex-1 spacer between the title group and the action group.

gates.title: Header Actions Survive A Narrow Viewport
gates.rule: Labels collapse to icons or into an overflow control below the breakpoint, and the header never wraps into two rows of controls or pushes its title out of view.
gates.fix: Hide the label text at narrow widths with the icon carrying the action, keeping the accessible name.

gates.title: Header Controls Are Vertically Centred
gates.rule: The header row declares align-items: center with line-height 1 on the items that have intrinsic height. Default flex stretch makes a button taller than the title beside it and breaks the baseline.
gates.fix: Set align-items: center on the header row.

gates.title: Section Heads Stack, They Do Not Sit Beside
gates.rule: An eyebrow, number, or kicker goes directly above its heading in the same column, never in a column beside it. The side-by-side arrangement reads as a templated editorial tell within seconds. The same tell wearing a different shape: a big left-aligned headline with a small explainer paragraph floating in the section head's top-right corner, aligned to nothing. Stack it under the headline at a 65ch measure, or give the right column a real visual.
gates.fix: Flatten the head wrapper to a single column, and move any floating corner paragraph under the headline.

gates.title: Header Height Is A Token
gates.rule: The header's height is a named value, because sticky offsets, scroll padding, and anchor margins all have to agree with it. Three hardcoded copies of 64px drift the first time one changes.
gates.fix: Define a header height token and reference it from the header, the offsets, and the scroll padding.

gates.title: Breadcrumbs And Back Sit In The Header
gates.rule: Where a page is reached from somewhere, the way back lives in the header at a consistent position, not invented per page.
gates.fix: Add the back or breadcrumb slot to the shared header component.
